Subject: Intro / security questions after demo

Hi Marissa / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team was impressed with the performance stats and the routing/cost controls. Before we move forward on procurement we need to validate a few security/compliance items on our side (FinBank InfoSec). High-level asks:

- SOC 2 status and most recent attestation
- Encryption in transit and at-rest specifics (algorithms, TLS versions)
- Key management options: customer-managed keys (CMK), HSM support, BYOK possibilities
- Any HIPAA/GDPR compatibility notes you can share

I'm attaching our vendor security questionnaire (fillable) and the InfoSec team would like Redwood to complete it. Can you confirm who from your side will own the questionnaire and whether we need a separate technical deep-dive for KMS/HSM details?

Also, can you confirm if Redwood offers an option where keys are customer-controlled (we want to avoid Redwood having plaintext access to master keys)?

Appreciate a short reply with SOC2 attestation and a pointer to any KMK docs you have.

Thanks,
Lydia Gomez
Head of Vendor Risk — FinBank
lydia.gomez@finbank.com

Attachment: Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Fillable.docx (fillable questionnaire)

Date: 2026-04-12T17:22:00Z

Hi Lydia — great to meet you today, and thanks for the clear list.

Short answers up-front:
- SOC 2: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified (report period through 2025). I attached the attestation PDF.
- In transit: All traffic uses TLS 1.2+ (we recommend TLS 1.3 where supported). Mutual TLS is available for dedicated/private deployments.
- At rest: Data is encrypted using AES-256; customer data is segmented per-tenant in Dedicated/Private.
- Keys / KMS: We support customer-managed key (CMK) options depending on deployment: Hosted API (standard) supports CMK via cloud KMS envelope encryption for enterprise plans; Dedicated and Private give you more flexible BYOK/HSM integration and isolated key proxies. I'll attach our KMK integration spec for details.
- HIPAA/GDPR: We support HIPAA-compliant configurations (BAA available) and have GDPR contracts/data residency options — happy to share specifics.

Next steps / owners:
1) I'll assign Aditya (cc'd) to handle the KMS/HSM technical follow-up and the vendor questionnaire.
2) If you can confirm the primary security contact who will own the questionnaire (Aaron or someone on sec team), we'll complete and return it.
3) Proposed times for a technical deep dive (KMS/HSM/keys): Tues 2026-04-14 09:00-11:00 ET or Wed 2026-04-15 14:00-16:00 ET. Let us know what works.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Attestation_2025.pdf, KMK_Integration_Specs.xlsx

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa / Aditya —

Thanks for the quick replies and the SOC2 attestation. A few follow-ups from InfoSec after a brief review:

1) Key ownership & access: we need to validate that Redwood cannot decrypt customer master keys or access plaintext CMKs. Please confirm whether Redwood ever has access to unwrapped customer CMKs in the hosted setup. If you offer envelope encryption, clarify the separation of duties and whether keys reside in customer-controlled KMS (e.g., our AWS KMS account) or Redwood-managed KMS.

2) HSM support: Does Redwood support HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM / HSM appliance) for Dedicated/Private? Any published architecture docs would help.

3) Key rotation and revocation: what's the typical rotation cadence supported, and do you support rapid revocation if a key is compromised?

4) Zero-access model: can you describe your zero-access controls for plaintext customer data and keys, plus auditing (key use logs, vault access logs, CloudTrail/Stackdriver retention windows)?

5) Retention and deletion: how is key material handled when a customer terminates service — is there an automated key delete/crypto-wipe process?

We also need you to fill and return the attached questionnaire. Please let us know who on your team will own the questionnaire completion. We'll need a technical call with your infra/security engineer.

Thanks,
Aaron Lee
Senior Manager, Information Security — FinBank
aaron.lee@finbank.com

From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Intro / security questions after demo — technical answers and next steps

Aaron / Lydia / Marissa — thanks, happy to take point on the technical follow-up and the questionnaire. Below are direct answers to Aaron's bullets plus proposed next steps.

1) Does Redwood ever have access to plaintext CMKs in hosted setup?
Short answer: No. For enterprise customers that require customer-managed keys on the hosted plan we use an envelope encryption pattern where the customer controls the root CMK in their cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS external account) and we maintain a service-side data encryption key that is wrapped by the customer's CMK. Redwood does not have access to the unwrapped customer CMK, and key material used to encrypt customer data at rest is stored encrypted and only ever unwrapped within a transient, HSM-backed key proxy (if configured) or within tenant-isolated runtime for Dedicated/Private.

2) HSM support / BYOK:
- Dedicated: supports CloudHSM and on-prem HSM integration (PKCS#11) and can be configured to use customer HSM appliances for CMK storage.
- Private: full BYOK and HSM integration — customers can provision keys into their HSM and we integrate via a key proxy layer.
- Hosted (enterprise plan): support for Customer-Managed Keys via cloud KMS envelope encryption and optional External Key Store (XKS) patterns (where the HSM is in the customer account).

3) Key rotation & revocation:
- Rotation: we support scheduled rotation (recommended 90 days) and immediate rotation via API.
- Revocation: keys can be disabled/revoked in the customer's KMS; for Dedicated/Private we can enforce immediate rekey and crypto-wipe of cached DEKs. We provide playbooks for emergency rotation and support one-off escalations.

4) Zero-access controls & auditing:
- Access: Redwood follows a least-privilege model; plaintext keys are never persisted in long-term storage. For HSM-backed workflows, cryptographic operations occur inside HSM or an ephemeral in-memory key proxy.
- Auditing: Key usage logs are captured via cloud audit trails (e.g., AWS CloudTrail) and are available to customers for the retention window you choose. We surface key use events in the Redwood Console and can export to your SIEM.

5) Retention & deletion:
- When a customer terminates service we provide a documented crypto-wipe process. For CMKs you control, deletion is performed in your KMS; for DEKs managed by Redwood we perform authenticated deletion and overwrite per our crypto-wipe policy.

Questionnaire & scheduling: We'll fill out the Vendor_Security_Questionnaire and return it no later than 2026-04-16 EOD. Proposed times for a technical deep dive (KMS/HSM architecture + runbook review):
- Tue 2026-04-14 10:00-11:30 ET (we can do a shorter focused session on key flow)
- Wed 2026-04-15 15:00-16:30 ET (deep dive with Rishi and infra)

Can you confirm a preferred slot and who will join from FinBank (network/security/ops)? I'll attach the KMK spec again here for your engineers.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
